page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v7 is an AMD-based instance classified under the general-purpose Daldsv7 family, configured specifically with a reduced memory-to-core ratio and direct local storage. The virtual machine provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz, supported by Hyper-V virtualization. Compute capabilities are enhanced by vector execution support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. It is paired with 96.0 GB of system RAM, allocating exactly 2.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates 2,835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and data processing throughput. In raw compute assessments, the instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 77,885.39, with extended instruction performance scoring 79,944.97 and encryption reaching 60,005.04. Compression benchmarks show top-tier execution, recording 41.5 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.1 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside 315.94 GB/sec across multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tasks. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 5,011.43 GB/sec in cached small-block reads, 154.83 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads, and 102.98 GB/sec in large-block writes.

Real-world application tests highlight effective handling of data pipelines and network serving. PassMark database operations reached 28,576.08, while Redis SET operations achieved 77.15 million operations per second. Static web serving maintained a throughput of 53.8 GB/sec. For CPU-based machine learning inference, the instance processed 4,366.28 prompt tokens per second and 397.95 generation tokens per second on lightweight 135M models, alongside 36.02 generation tokens per second on medium 7B models.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D48alds_v7 lies in its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, which provides less memory head-room than standard 1:4 general-purpose instances. However, this yields high compute density and localized disk throughput, making it cost-efficient for compute-heavy batch tasks, data compression pipelines, caching tiers, and high-concurrency web serving that benefit from fast NVMe storage without requiring massive memory allocations.

Allocated with 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and bundled with 2,835 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, it features a compute-dense 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Supported by AVX-512 and VNNI extensions, benchmarks display top-tier data handling, achieving 41.5 GB/sec in gzip compression and 77.15 million Redis SET operations per second. PassMark CPU performance is strong at 77,885.39, supplemented by 53.8 GB/sec web serving throughput. Lacking a GPU, the instance is structurally engineered for high-concurrency tasks requiring fast local IOPS and CPU efficiency, such as large web servers, data manipulation pipelines, compression tasks, and localized caching tiers.
